title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.

examples.explanation: The element 1 occurs at indices 0 and 3.

hints: Think about what data structure allows O(1) lookups.
A set can track which elements you've already seen.

title: Valid Anagram
description:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.

An anagram is a word formed by rearranging the letters of another word, using all the original letters exactly once.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: What if you count the frequency of each character?
Compare character counts between both strings using a hash map or Counter.

title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
hints: For each number, what complement would you need to reach the target?
A hash map can store each number's index for O(1) complement lookups.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: How can you create a key that is the same for all anagrams of a word?
Sorting each string gives the same result for all anagrams. Use it as a hash map key.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.
constraints: k is in the range [1, number of unique elements]
The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
hints: Count the frequency of each element first.
You can use bucket sort where the index represents the frequency.
